diagnosis.summary: The product-service DynamoDB table is experiencing severe read throttling, with 533 read throttle events and 297 throttled requests per minute against a baseline of zero for both. Read capacity consumed has risen approximately 151x, from 449.3 to 67,974 RCU/min. No 5xx errors have appeared at either product-service or payment-service so far.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the Products table is the most likely root cause.
evidence: product-service read_throttle_events rose from 0 to 533/min and throttled_requests rose from 0 to 297/min, both from a baseline of zero.
product-service db_consumed_read_capacity surged from 449.3 to 67,974 RCU/min, a roughly 151x increase.
product-service p99_latency_ms rose from 9.587 ms to 41.864 ms (about 4.4x), while p95_latency_ms moved only from 6.56 ms to 6.81 ms, showing throttling pressure concentrated at the tail.
product-service write_throttle_events remain at 0; throttling is confined to reads only.
error_rate_5xx is 0 for both product-service and payment-service, indicating no requests have yet exhausted retries.
payment-service request_rate rose from 0.9433 to 2.0833 rps, approximately 2.2x its baseline.
recommended_actions: Raise the Products table provisioned read capacity or switch it to on-demand mode to relieve the current throttling immediately.

Check db_consumed_read_capacity against the Products table provisioned read rate to quantify how far over capacity reads are running, and inspect whether GET /products calls are scanning the full table on every request.
Reduce per-call read cost on GET /products by adding pagination (a limit and next-page token) or caching the product list inside the Lambda function between invocations.
Keep the SDK retry configuration unchanged during the incident; reducing retry attempts would convert the current tail latency into 5xx errors.
After each change, recheck read_throttle_events and db_latency_ms_p95 to confirm throttling is subsiding.
